newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Three Tenors in court battle over Swedish concert.
newsitem.headline: Three Tenors in court battle over Swedish concert.

text.p: Top opera tenors Domingo, Carreras and Pavarotti are locked in a court battle with organisers of a Swedish concert who refused to pay them in full because two of them were alleged to have broken a contract.
Organisers of a Three Tenors' concert in Gothenburg this summer say two of the trio, Jose Carreras and Luciano Pavarotti, breached contract by slipping away from a gala autograph-signing banquet.
But concert promoter, the Tenor Concerts Partnership, is taking legal action against the organisers, Sweden's Hellmi Promotion AB, in Frankfurt, Germany, seeking full payment.
Swedish concert-goers paid 7,950 crowns ($1,200) for front-row seats at the concert and a banquet which organisers had promised would be attended by the musicians.
But only Placido Domingo stayed through the dinner, which was attended by around 700 people.
"We had a paragraph in the contract that said they should appear at a banquet and sign autographs for the people who paid for the dinner," Hellmi's managing director Mikael Hellqvist said.
"They actually left the banquet before everybody was even seated."
A Swedish high court told Reuters on Wednesday that it had upheld a decision by a Swedish lower court to freeze Hellmi Promotion's accounts until the case was decided in Germany.
Hellqvist saw this only as a minor setback. "The main case will come up in the court in Frankfurt," he said.
Hellqvist said the company had had to refund some money to disappointed guests.
Swedish media said Hellmi Productions had already paid 33 million crowns to the singers but had stopped payments to the Tenor Concerts Partnership of another 18 million crowns.
Hellqvist declined to confirm the figures.
